candidate.flaw_one_line: The @better-auth/sso plugin persists user-supplied OIDC endpoint URLs (authorization/token/userInfo/jwks) at provider registration and update without any origin or routability check, then fetches them server-side at OIDC callback time. An authenticated user who may manage SSO can point an endpoint at an internal host (loopback, RFC1918, link-local, cloud metadata) and coerce the server into contacting it (non-blind SSRF).

verified.exploit_entry_point: HTTP POST /api/auth/sign-in/sso triggers GET /api/auth/sso/callback/:providerId, which performs server-side fetches to the stored token/userInfo/jwks endpoints. Those endpoints are saved by POST /api/auth/sso/register (skipDiscovery or endpoint override) and POST /api/auth/sso/update-provider.
verified.shape: DeepSeek shape 2 (Hadi, data producer off the check's path): the CHECK the report points at is the callback's server-side fetch; the DATA PRODUCER is the registration/update handler that persists the endpoints (different files, packages/sso/src/routes/sso.ts and providers.ts). The check does not call the producer; the endpoints reach the fetch via save-and-reload (JSON.stringify at registration -> safeJsonParse at callback). The callback's pre-existing validation (validateDiscoveryUrl / normalizeDiscoveryUrls, packages/sso/src/oidc/discovery.ts) runs only on the runtime-discovery path, which stored skip-discovery providers bypass (needsRuntimeDiscovery is false when token+jwks+auth are present), so a fix placed on that path leaves the stored-data path open (proved by callback_discovery_path_only.patch).
variants: token endpoint: skip-discovery registration saves tokenEndpoint=internal; callback's code exchange (validateAuthorizationCode) fetches it (security/endpoint_contact::token exchange)
user-info endpoint: skip-discovery saves userInfoEndpoint=internal; callback fetches it after a successful token exchange (security/endpoint_contact::user-info fetch)
key (jwks) endpoint: skip-discovery saves jwksEndpoint=internal and no userInfoEndpoint; callback fetches keys to verify the ID token (security/endpoint_contact::key (jwks) fetch)

update route: an existing allow-listed provider is edited (POST /sso/update-provider, mergeOIDCConfig) to move an endpoint onto an internal host (security/endpoint_contact::updating an existing provider)

discovery override: registration WITHOUT skipDiscovery still lets a supplied tokenEndpoint take precedence over the discovered value and be stored unvalidated (security/endpoint_contact::explicit endpoint override)
verified.project_tests_run: The repo's own @better-auth/sso suite was run on the vulnerable commit (packages/sso: 22 passing in src/oidc.test.ts). The vulnerable tree, the reference fix and every check patch were run offline with the hidden suite via vitest (node 24, pnpm 10.30.2, memoryAdapter + oauth2-mock-server + loopback listeners): vulnerable 0/5 security + 5/5 functional; reference 5/5 + 5/5.

patch_checks.note: DeepSeek-shaped wrong fix: adds the routability guard to the runtime-discovery validation path (where the server fetches) honouring trustedOrigins, but stored skip-discovery endpoints never traverse that path, so all 5 attacks still reach the internal host; functional all pass
wrong_resource: validates the neighbouring discoveryEndpoint field instead of the per-endpoint URLs the server actually fetches
unlisted_route: reference fix minus the update-provider site; the merge/update route to the same stored sink stays open
refuse_all: registration rejects every OIDC provider; secure but legitimate SSO is dead

adjacent_api / over-restriction: hardens the shared discovery validator to reject non-routable hosts ignoring trustedOrigins, breaking a legitimately allow-listed internal IdP (the discovery sibling's stated behaviour)
independent correct fix at a different valid layer: validates each stored endpoint at the callback fetch sites (honouring trustedOrigins) instead of at registration; scores 1.0
reference write-path validation plus a defense-in-depth guard at the callback fetch sites; scores 1.0

notes: source = mined. No code was planted into /app; the Dockerfile checks out the unmodified vulnerable commit. All traps are real pre-existing gaps in better-auth. The blind pass patch and build/<slug>/FAIRNESS.md are produced by independent agents (not in this manifest yet); static will flag both as missing, which is expected per builder/BRIEF-trap-stack.md rule 6.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the property is 'no outbound request to a disallowed host', not a specific refusal form; a fix that blocks by throwing still prevents the contact and still passes, and legitimate registration/sign-in is guarded by the functional tests, so there is no distinct wrong fix in this class
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: a single actor and a single direction (the server's outbound request to a provider endpoint); there are no peer roles or request directions to split
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protected operation is the write that saves provider endpoints; both write entry points (register and update) are exercised, and there is no read-vs-write split on the sink
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: a saved per-endpoint URL is fetched verbatim with no normalising or adjusting step between the attacker value and the request; the decision is made on that same value
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the allow decision is made on the host as parsed by the same WHATWG URL parser the fetch uses, so there is no second spelling on which the guard and the sink could disagree
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the allow decision is local (public-routability plus the operator's trustedOrigins allow-list), with no external authority that could return no result and make the guard fail open

traps.shape: DeepSeek shape 2 (data producer off the check's path): the endpoints are produced/persisted by the registration handler and reach the callback's fetch via save-and-reload; the callback's existing validation lives on the runtime-discovery path that stored skip-discovery providers bypass

traps.realistic_because: Unmodified upstream code. skipDiscovery is a documented feature for IdPs without a discovery document; the discovery branch already routes URLs through an origin check, so the skip branch not doing so reads as an oversight on a secondary path, and the fetch happens far from where the endpoints are saved.

traps.shape: merged / defaults route to the same sink (MiMo, different file): the update-provider handler merges supplied endpoints into the stored config via mergeOIDCConfig and persists them, reaching the same callback fetch sink

traps.realistic_because: Unmodified upstream code in a different file from registration. Editing a provider is the standard management operation; a fix applied only to the registration handler the report points at leaves the update route open, which is exactly the upstream patch's second site.
